entities.summary:
Desiderio da Settignano (1420-16 Jan 1464) was an Italian Renaissance sculptor active in north Italy, particularly in Florence. He is known for his contributions to the development of Renaissance sculpture, particularly in the use of terracotta and bronze. Da Settignano's works include the famous 'St. Sebastian' and 'St. Catherine,' which showcase his mastery of human anatomy and emotional expression.

 His significance lies in his role as a bridge between the Gothic and Renaissance styles, influencing artists such as Michelangelo and Donatello. The Medici family commissioned many of his works, solidifying his position as a leading figure in the Renaissance art scene.

 Da Settignano's legacy can be seen in the many artists who followed in his footsteps, including Michelangelo and Raphael, who further developed the techniques and styles he pioneered.

 In his time, da Settignano was celebrated for his technical skill and innovative use of materials, earning him the nickname 'Ferro' (Iron) for his ability to shape and mold terracotta and bronze.

 His contributions to the development of Renaissance sculpture have had a lasting impact on the art world, ensuring his place among the greatest sculptors of all time.

 As a testament to his enduring influence, da Settignano's works continue to inspire artists and art historians alike, a true reflection of his masterful craft.
